# Companies can contribute to happiness at work, but they are not solely responsible.

**Organizations can create a conducive environment for fostering happiness at work by promoting good treatment, allowing employees to apply their strengths, and recognizing the meaning of their work within the company.**

**Expressing gratitude, acknowledging achievements, being kind, smiling, among other practices, are some of the actions that are within the employee's autonomy and, according to analysts, could increase happiness at work.**

- [Start](https://www.eafit.edu.co/)
- [News](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias)
- Companies can contribute to happiness at work, but they are not solely responsible.

![Image: Companies can contribute to happiness at work, but they are not solely responsible](https://universidadeafit.widen.net/content/e56cfee4-220c-42ac-bd8e-74e63cbe6f16/web/felicidadeneltrabajo.jpg?crop=yes&k=c&w=823&h=450&itok=ru-Rxieo)

Happiness at work is a goal that people must pursue for themselves, although the environment is a facilitator.

Are you happy at your job? Faced with the idea of ​​happiness as something fleeting and elusive, dependent on external circumstances—like the luck of having a "good boss"—analysts at EAFIT clarify that this concept is much more complex, as it requires a high level of individual commitment, while the role of companies focuses on generating certain conditions that make the employee feel good.

So, what does happiness at work mean? Camilo Álvarez Lince, Talent Development Leader at EAFIT, explains it this way: “Happiness is a broad and profound concept that shouldn't be confused, as it sometimes is, with mere joy or satisfaction. But since we're talking about happiness in a specific context—work—I would venture to define it as a state of well-being and fulfillment.” Beyond the administrative rhetoric that distorts the meaning of happiness at work, for Camilo it's about having adequate physical and psychological conditions, as well as finding purpose in what each person does.

Alejandro Sanín Posada, professor of the Master's Program in Organizational Human Development at the EAFIT School of Management and founding partner of Siete Human and Organizational Management, agrees that there are many myths surrounding happiness. One of these is that it is an emotion, but his research has found that it is a long-term cognitive and affective phenomenon, composed of three dimensions applicable to work: pleasure, experiencing positive emotions; gratification, the feeling of being able to put skills and strengths into practice; and meaning, having a reason to act.

###### What role do companies play?

Individuals are responsible for their own happiness, but employers have responsibilities regarding working conditions, such as the physical environment, workload, climate, and other related issues. In this regard, Camilo points out that some companies even want to expand this scope, but he cautions that care must be taken to respect personal boundaries and avoid coercive actions.

While happiness is not a decision, as has been simplified in some scenarios, but a conscious and personal effort that requires cultivating habits such as gratitude, identifying achievements, exercising, being kind, applying strengths, smiling, having social support, among others, companies have the opportunity to establish actions that invite and promote practices that favor happiness.

“Three things can be done: create a context of good treatment, cooperation, respect and mutual help; generate a connection between work and people's strengths through selection, training and leadership processes; and, finally, foster scenarios where people can build a sense of why they do what they do, whether it is from having, being or transcending,” says Professor Alejandro.

In a society that recently faced a pandemic, the idea of ​​not postponing dreams has spread, and that, together with the awareness of the finiteness of life and its unpredictable changes, makes people especially value the environments and roles in which they feel most connected and find flexibility.

In this regard, Sebastián U Chinkovsky, co-founder of the startup Newo, highlights the importance of creating suitable scenarios and overcoming the perspective of work as an obligation, to understand it as an experience that encompasses not only the physical space, but also the relationships that are established, as he promotes in his venture.

###### The challenge for entrepreneurs and freelancers

Freelancers and entrepreneurs are characterized by a special connection to their work, stemming from knowledge and a sense of purpose. Despite this, they may also miss the immersion in a system of organizational culture, identity, and camaraderie. “This population is underserved, and that's where community and platform models become attractive, even to companies themselves, because they want their employees to have these kinds of experiences,” Sebastián points out.

For those without formal employment or who choose to start their own business, the challenge of finding happiness at work is much greater, as well-being can be sacrificed for the sake of a better future. In this regard, experts point out that the relationship between money and happiness disappears once basic needs are met.

Por tanto, la recomendación es buscar y lograr un balance entre los ingresos y el bienestar, debido a que las acciones actuales tendrán efectos en el mediano y largo plazo. El autocuidado es fundamental para llegar al puerto deseado sin desilusión o con afecciones graves de salud que impidan disfrutar de la vida. ​ ​

###### Virus contra bacterias, la propuesta para el sector porcino de PhageLife desde EAFIT

En una granja porcina, una infección bacteriana puede poner en riesgo la salud de los animales y la productividad del negocio. Además, el problema se vuelve más complejo cuando las bacterias dejan de responder a los antibióticos que antes permitían combatirlas. Para explorar otra vía, la empresa [PhageLife](https://phagelife.co/) desarrolla soluciones personalizadas con bacteriófagos, virus naturales capaces de eliminar bacterias específicas.

metadata.ogDescription: ​¿Es feliz en su trabajo? Ante la idea de felicidad como un asunto fugaz y escurridizo, que depende de circunstancias externas —como la suerte de contar con un “buen jefe”—, analistas de EAFIT aclaran que este concepto es mucho más complejo, ya que exige un compromiso individual alto, mientras que el papel de las empresas se centra en la generación de ciertas condiciones que hagan sentir bien al empleado.
